groups.title: Testing strategy for a T3 application
groups.question: You want confidence that your tRPC procedures and key user flows work before every deploy. Explain how you would test a T3 app at the API level and in the browser.

followUps.Unit testing tRPC procedures with the ca: How can you test a tRPC procedure without running an HTTP server?
followUps.End-to-end testing with Playwright: brow: What does an end-to-end test with Playwright catch that unit tests miss?

evidence.text: tRPC lets tests call procedures directly through a caller.
Tests pass a context with a fake session and a test or mocked database.
This checks the procedure's logic, including unauthorized and invalid input cases.

notEnough: Only saying you unit test procedures.

evidence.text: Playwright drives a real browser through the full app.
It checks that frontend, API and database work together.
It is best used for a few critical flows like sign-in and checkout.

notEnough: Only saying it tests the whole app.

groups.title: Production deployment concepts for Next.js on Vercel
groups.question: Your T3 app is deployed on Vercel and some pages are fast while others are slow on the first request. Explain how Vercel runs the different parts of a Next.js app.

followUps.Vercel's build output: static, SSR, and: Where do static pages, server-rendered pages and edge code run on Vercel?

evidence.text: Statically generated pages are served from a CDN.
Server-rendered pages and API routes run in serverless functions.
Edge runtime code runs on servers close to users with a more limited set of APIs.

groups.title: Writing and running tests for a T3 project
groups.question: You are setting up Vitest for a T3 project and testing a component that loads posts through tRPC. Explain the configuration and how the test should be written.

followUps.Vitest configuration for a Next.js proje: What needs configuring for Vitest to understand your imports and components?
followUps.Testing React components with Testing Li: How would you test a component that loads data through tRPC?

evidence.text: Path aliases from tsconfig must be added to the Vitest config so imports resolve.
A React plugin handles JSX.
Component tests need a browser-like environment such as jsdom.
Render the component with Testing Library.
Fake the API responses, for example with MSW, so the test does not hit a real server.
Find elements by role, interact with user events and check the visible result.

notEnough: Only saying you render the component.

groups.title: Deploying T3 to Vercel with a production database
groups.question: You are deploying your T3 app to Vercel with a production database, and a teammate wants to put the database URL in a NEXT_PUBLIC variable to fix an error. Explain how environment variables and migrations should be handled.

followUps.Environment variables in Vercel: build-t: Why must the database URL never be a NEXT_PUBLIC variable?
followUps.Running prisma migrate deploy in the Ver: How do database migrations get applied when you deploy?

evidence.text: NEXT_PUBLIC variables are inlined into the browser bundle at build time.
Anything in the bundle can be read by any user.
Secrets like the database URL stay server-only and are read at runtime.

notEnough: Only saying not to expose secrets.

evidence.text: prisma migrate deploy applies pending migrations to the production database.
It runs in the build or release step before the new code serves traffic.
migrate dev is for development only and must not be used against production.

notEnough: Only saying migrations run on deploy.
